title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

We propose SVEAD that leverages stochastic Voronoi dia-

core contribution lies in recognizing that local anomalies,
though indistinguishable under global analysis, become con-
spicuous when the data space is decomposed into restricted

averaging reduces variance and ensures robustness, and
the dual-factor scoring mechanism creates clear separation

achieves state-of-the-art performance with linear time com-
plexity, outperforming 12 baselines. SVEAD’s effectiveness
across global, local, and dependency anomaly types, com-
bined with its computational efficiency, makes it a practical
solution for large-scale anomaly detection applications.

"""Core SVEAD algorithm (paper Section 4, Algorithm 1).

Requirements implemented here:
  R1  anchors sampled uniformly without replacement
  R2  assignment to nearest anchor by Euclidean distance
  R3  within-cell score = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean
  R4  per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed before scoring
  R5  singleton cells are skipped in that partition
  R6  aggregation by arithmetic mean over the partitions that scored the point
  R11 implicit Voronoi: only nearest-anchor queries, no cell boundaries
  R12 chunked O(n*m*d*t) implementation, linear in n
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import time

import numpy as np

CHUNK_ROWS = 4096


def _rng(seed: int, m: int, k: int) -> np.random.Generator:
    """Deterministic generator for (seed, m, partition k)."""
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence([int(seed), int(m), int(k)]))


def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Uniform sampling without replacement -> distinct anchor row indices (R1)."""
    if m > n:
        raise ValueError("m (%d) cannot exceed n (%d)" % (m, n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=int(m), replace=False)


def assign_cells(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS):
    """Assign every row of X to its nearest anchor (implicit Voronoi, R2/R11).

    Returns (cell_ids int64 [n], delta float64 [n]) with delta the Euclidean
    distance to the assigned anchor.  Ties resolve to the lowest anchor index
    (numpy argmin).
    """
    n = X.shape[0]
    m = A.shape[0]
    A2 = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", A, A)
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for s in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        e = min(s + chunk_rows, n)
        B = X[s:e]
        d2 = A2[None, :] - 2.0 * (B @ A.T)
        d2 += np.einsum("ij,ij->i", B, B)[:, None]
        idx = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)
        cell[s:e] = idx
        delta[s:e] = np.sqrt(np.maximum(d2[np.arange(e - s), idx], 0.0))
    return cell, delta


def cell_stats(cell: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int):
    """Per-cell delta_max and delta_mean over all points assigned to the cell (R4).

    The anchor itself is a member of its cell with distance 0 (it is sampled from X),
    so singleton cells (|C|=1) have delta_max = delta_mean = 0 and are skipped later.
    """
    counts = np.bincount(cell, minlength=m).astype(np.float64)
    sums = np.bincount(cell, weights=delta, minlength=m)
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    np.maximum.at(dmax, cell, delta)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        dmean = np.where(counts > 0, sums / np.maximum(counts, 1.0), 0.0)
    return counts, dmax, dmean


def score_partition(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS):
    """Per-partition scores; NaN where the point's cell is a singleton (R3/R5)."""
    cell, delta = assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows=chunk_rows)
    counts, dmax, dmean = cell_stats(cell, delta, A.shape[0])
    valid = counts[cell] > 1
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        denom = np.where(dmax[cell] > 0, dmax[cell], np.nan)
        s = (delta / denom) * dmean[cell]
    s[~valid] = np.nan
    s[~np.isfinite(s)] = np.nan
    diag = {
        "cell_sizes": counts,
        "n_singleton_cells": int((counts == 1).sum()),
        "n_empty_cells": int((counts == 0).sum()),
    }
    return s, diag


def svead_score(X: np.ndarray, m: int, t: int = 100, seed: int = 1,
                chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS, return_diag: bool = False):
    """Full SVEAD ensemble score for X (R1-R6, R12).

    f(x) = mean over the partitions that scored x; partitions in which x falls in a
    singleton cell are skipped for that point (R5); a point skipped by all t partitions
    receives score 0 (degenerate guard, assumption A7).
    """
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    acc = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    cnt = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    diag = {
        "cell_sizes": [],
        "n_singleton_cells": [],
        "per_partition_seconds": [],
    }
    for k in range(t):
        rng = _rng(seed, m, k)
        A = X[sample_anchors(n, m, rng)]
        tk = time.perf_counter()
        s, d = score_partition(X, A, chunk_rows=chunk_rows)
        ok = np.isfinite(s)
        acc[ok] += s[ok]
        cnt[ok] += 1
        diag["per_partition_seconds"].append(time.perf_counter() - tk)
        if return_diag:
            diag["cell_sizes"].append(d["cell_sizes"])
            diag["n_singleton_cells"].append(d["n_singleton_cells"])
    scores = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    scored = cnt > 0
    scores[scored] = acc[scored] / cnt[scored]
    diag["seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    diag["skipped_fraction"] = float((~scored).mean())
    diag["mean_partitions_used"] = float(cnt.mean())
    if return_diag and diag["cell_sizes"]:
        sizes = np.concatenate(diag["cell_sizes"])
        diag["cell_size_mean"] = float(sizes.mean())
        diag["cell_size_max"] = int(sizes.max())
    return (scores, diag) if return_diag else scores


def svead_score_div_t(X: np.ndarray, m: int, t: int = 100, seed: int = 1):
    """Sensitivity variant: skipped partitions contribute 0 and the sum is divided by t
    (literal Algorithm 1 line 20).  Reported as a robustness check only."""
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    acc = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for k in range(t):
        rng = _rng(seed, m, k)
        A = X[sample_anchors(n, m, rng)]
        s, _ = score_partition(X, A)
        ok = np.isfinite(s)
        acc[ok] += s[ok]
    return acc / float(t)

"""Smoke test: tiny end-to-end proof of the SVEAD data flow.

Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% injected Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3.
Part B: the real cardio table, m=8, t=5 (checks determinism and runtime).
Run:  python experiments/smoke_test.py
"""
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import load_cardio, roc_auc, svead_score, standardize  # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import _rng, sample_anchors  # noqa: E402


def part_a():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    n, d = 300, 6
    X = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=(n, d))
    k = 30
    X[-k:] = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=(k, d)) * 0.3 + 8.0
    y = np.zeros(n, dtype=int)
    y[-k:] = 1
    s = svead_score(X, m=4, t=3, seed=1)
    assert s.shape == (n,), s.shape
    assert np.isfinite(s).all(), "non-finite scores"
    assert (s >= 0).all(), "negative scores"
    auc = roc_auc(s, y)
    print("part A: synthetic %dx%d m=4 t=3 -> AUC-ROC %.4f (%.4f..%.4f)"
          % (n, d, auc, s.min(), s.max()))
    assert auc > 0.8, "synthetic AUC-ROC too low: %.4f" % auc
    return auc


def part_b():
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    X, y, info = load_cardio()
    assert info["signature_ok"], info
    Xs = standardize(X)
    s1 = svead_score(Xs, m=8, t=5, seed=1)
    s2 = svead_score(Xs, m=8, t=5, seed=1)
    assert s1.shape == (1831,)
    assert np.array_equal(s1, s2), "not deterministic for identical (m, seed)"
    auc = roc_auc(s1, y)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    print("part B: cardio n=%d d=%d anomalies=%d m=8 t=5 -> AUC-ROC %.4f (%.2fs, deterministic)"
          % (info["n"], info["d"], info["n_anomalies"], auc, dt))
    assert dt < 60, "smoke test too slow: %.1fs" % dt
    return auc


def anchors_check():
    n, m = 1831, 256
    for seed in range(20):
        r = _rng(seed + 1, m, 0)
        idx = sample_anchors(n, m, r)
        assert len(idx) == m and len(np.unique(idx)) == m, "anchor sampling not distinct"
    print("anchors: 20 random (m=256, seed) draws are distinct and of size m")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    a = part_a()
    anchors_check()
    b = part_b()
    print("SMOKE TEST OK: synthetic AUC-ROC %.4f, cardio AUC-ROC %.4f" % (a, b))

"""Cardio experiment: SVEAD with t=100, m grid {2^1..2^8}, 5 repeated runs.

Writes results/raw_cardio.json and results/per_m_table.csv.

Usage: python experiments/run_cardio.py [--t 100] [--repeats 5] [--out results]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import (auc_pr_ap, auc_pr_trapz, load_cardio, roc_auc,  # noqa: E402
                   standardize, summarize)
from svead.svead_core import svead_score, svead_score_div_t  # noqa: E402

M_GRID = [2 ** p for p in range(1, 9)]  # {2^1, ..., 2^8}, paper Sec 5.1 (R7)
T_DEFAULT = 100
REPEATS_DEFAULT = 5
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]


def run_grid(X, y, m_grid, t, seeds, tag=""):
    records = []
    for m in m_grid:
        for seed in seeds:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            s, diag = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed, return_diag=True)
            secs = time.perf_counter() - t0
            rec = {
                "m": int(m),
                "seed": int(seed),
                "t": int(t),
                "auc_roc": roc_auc(s, y),
                "auc_pr_ap": auc_pr_ap(s, y),
                "auc_pr_trapz": auc_pr_trapz(s, y),
                "seconds": secs,
                "skipped_fraction": diag["skipped_fraction"],
                "mean_partitions_used": diag["mean_partitions_used"],
                "cell_size_mean": diag.get("cell_size_mean"),
                "cell_size_max": diag.get("cell_size_max"),
                "n_singleton_cells_mean": float(np.mean(diag["n_singleton_cells"])),
                "variant": tag,
            }
            records.append(rec)
            print("  m=%3d seed=%d auc_roc=%.4f auc_pr=%.4f %.2fs skip=%.4f"
                  % (m, seed, rec["auc_roc"], rec["auc_pr_ap"], secs, rec["skipped_fraction"]),
                  flush=True)
    return records


def per_m_summary(records):
    out = []
    for m in sorted({r["m"] for r in records}):
        rs = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        out.append({
            "m": m,
            "auc_roc": summarize([r["auc_roc"] for r in rs]),
            "auc_pr_ap": summarize([r["auc_pr_ap"] for r in rs]),
            "auc_pr_trapz": summarize([r["auc_pr_trapz"] for r in rs]),
            "seconds_mean": float(np.mean([r["seconds"] for r in rs])),
            "auc_roc_per_seed": [r["auc_roc"] for r in rs],
            "auc_pr_per_seed": [r["auc_pr_ap"] for r in rs],
        })
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--t", type=int, default=T_DEFAULT)
    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=REPEATS_DEFAULT)
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=str, default="results")
    ap.add_argument("--m-grid", type=str, default=",".join(str(m) for m in M_GRID))
    ap.add_argument("--scaling", type=str, default="as_is",
                    choices=["as_is", "standardize", "both"],
                    help="as_is: use the ADBench artifact features unchanged (already standardized)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    m_grid = [int(v) for v in args.m_grid.split(",")]
    seeds = SEEDS[: args.repeats]

    X_raw, y, info = load_cardio()
    X_std = standardize(X_raw)
    print("cardio: %s" % info, flush=True)

    variants = {}
    if args.scaling in ("as_is", "both"):
        variants["as_is"] = X_raw
    if args.scaling in ("standardize", "both"):
        variants["standardize"] = X_std

    all_records = []
    for name, X in variants.items():
        print("grid (%s features):" % name, flush=True)
        recs = run_grid(X, y, m_grid, args.t, seeds, tag=name)
        all_records.extend(recs)

    primary = "as_is" if "as_is" in variants else list(variants)[0]
    primary_records = [r for r in all_records if r["variant"] == primary]
    summary = per_m_summary(primary_records)
    best = max(summary, key=lambda r: r["auc_roc"]["mean"])

    # Sensitivity: aggregation variant (divide by t) at the selected m.
    div_t = []
    for seed in seeds:
        s = svead_score_div_t(variants[primary], m=best["m"], t=args.t, seed=seed)
        div_t.append({"m": best["m"], "seed": seed, "auc_roc": roc_auc(s, y),
                      "auc_pr_ap": auc_pr_ap(s, y)})

    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {
        "dataset": "cardio",
        "dataset_info": info,
        "config": {"t": args.t, "m_grid": m_grid, "seeds": seeds, "repeats": args.repeats,
                   "primary_scaling": primary},
        "records": all_records,
        "per_m": summary,
        "per_m_per_variant": {name: per_m_summary([r for r in all_records if r["variant"] == name])
                              for name in variants},
        "selected_m": best["m"],
        "selected_m_rule": "argmax over m of the mean AUC-ROC across the repeats",
        "best_row": best,
        "div_t_variant_at_best_m": {
            "rows": div_t,
            "auc_roc": summarize([r["auc_roc"] for r in div_t]),
            "auc_pr_ap": summarize([r["auc_pr_ap"] for r in div_t]),
        },
        "wall_seconds": float(sum(r["seconds"] for r in all_records)),
    }
    with open(os.path.join(args.out, "raw_cardio.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(payload, fh, indent=1)

    with open(os.path.join(args.out, "per_m_table.csv"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("m,auc_roc_mean,auc_roc_std,auc_pr_mean,auc_pr_std,seconds_mean\n")
        for r in summary:
            fh.write("%d,%.6f,%.6f,%.6f,%.6f,%.3f\n"
                     % (r["m"], r["auc_roc"]["mean"], r["auc_roc"]["std"],
                        r["auc_pr_ap"]["mean"], r["auc_pr_ap"]["std"], r["seconds_mean"]))

    print("selected m=%d: AUC-ROC %.4f +- %.4f, AUC-PR %.4f +- %.4f"
          % (best["m"], best["auc_roc"]["mean"], best["auc_roc"]["std"],
             best["auc_pr_ap"]["mean"], best["auc_pr_ap"]["std"]))
    return payload


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Intermediate checks for the SVEAD reimplementation on cardio (plan step 7).

Run: python experiments/checks.py
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import load_cardio, roc_auc, standardize, svead_score  # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import _rng, assign_cells, cell_stats, sample_anchors  # noqa: E402

out = {}


def main():
    X, y, info = load_cardio()
    out["dataset_info"] = info
    assert X.shape == (1831, 21) and int(y.sum()) == 176, "dataset signature mismatch"
    assert np.isfinite(X).all(), "NaN/inf in features"
    assert abs(y.mean() - 0.0961) < 1e-3

    Z = standardize(X)
    out["standardized_means_absmax"] = float(np.abs(Z.mean(0)).max())
    out["standardized_stds_minmax"] = [float(Z.std(0).min()), float(Z.std(0).max())]
    assert out["standardized_means_absmax"] < 1e-9
    assert abs(out["standardized_stds_minmax"][0] - 1) < 1e-9

    # anchor sampling (R1)
    for seed in range(1, 21):
        idx = sample_anchors(X.shape[0], 256, _rng(seed, 256, 0))
        assert len(idx) == 256 and len(np.unique(idx)) == 256
    out["anchor_uniqueness_ok"] = True

    # cell diagnostics at m=256, seed=1 (R4/R5)
    rng = _rng(1, 256, 0)
    A = X[sample_anchors(X.shape[0], 256, rng)]
    cell, delta = assign_cells(X, A)
    counts, dmax, dmean = cell_stats(cell, delta, 256)
    out["cell_stats_m256"] = {
        "n_empty": int((counts == 0).sum()),
        "n_singleton": int((counts == 1).sum()),
        "cell_size_mean": float(counts.mean()),
        "cell_size_max": int(counts.max()),
        "delta_mean_min_nonempty": float(dmean[counts > 0].min()),
        "delta_max_min_nonempty": float(dmax[counts > 0].min()),
    }
    assert out["cell_stats_m256"]["n_singleton"] / 256 < 0.005, "too many singleton cells"

    # score sanity at the selected grid end (m=2) and a large m
    s2, diag2 = svead_score(X, m=2, t=100, seed=1, return_diag=True)
    assert np.isfinite(s2).all() and (s2 >= 0).all()
    out["score_stats_m2"] = {
        "min": float(s2.min()), "max": float(s2.max()), "mean": float(s2.mean()),
        "median": float(np.median(s2)),
        "anomaly_mean": float(s2[y == 1].mean()), "normal_mean": float(s2[y == 0].mean()),
        "skipped_fraction": diag2["skipped_fraction"],
        "mean_partitions_used": diag2["mean_partitions_used"],
        "auc_roc": roc_auc(s2, y),
    }
    assert out["score_stats_m2"]["anomaly_mean"] > out["score_stats_m2"]["normal_mean"]

    # kNN mean-distance baseline + Spearman correlation
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    k = 10
    nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=k + 1).fit(X)
    dist, _ = nn.kneighbors(X)
    knn_score = dist[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)
    from scipy.stats import spearmanr
    out["spearman_svead_vs_knn"] = float(spearmanr(s2, knn_score).statistic)
    out["auc_roc_knn_mean_dist"] = roc_auc(knn_score, y)
    assert out["spearman_svead_vs_knn"] > 0

    # isolation forest baseline
    from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
    for rs in (1, 2):
        iforest = IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=rs)
        iforest.fit(X)
        iso = -iforest.score_samples(X)
        out["auc_roc_iforest_rs%d" % rs] = roc_auc(iso, y)

    # scaling variant must not change the ranking materially
    s_std = svead_score(Z, m=2, t=100, seed=1)
    out["pearson_as_is_vs_standardized"] = float(np.corrcoef(s2, s_std)[0, 1])
    out["auc_roc_standardized_m2_seed1"] = roc_auc(s_std, y)

    # determinism
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    s_again = svead_score(X, m=2, t=100, seed=1)
    out["determinism_identical"] = bool(np.array_equal(s2, s_again))
    out["rerun_seconds_m2_t100"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    assert out["determinism_identical"]

    # timing probe at the largest grid point
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    svead_score(X, m=256, t=100, seed=1)
    out["seconds_m256_t100"] = time.perf_counter() - t0

    os.makedirs("results", exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join("results", "checks_cardio.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(out, fh, indent=1)
    print(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
    print("CHECKS OK")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Scalability measurement (paper Sec. 5.3 / Figure 5): 500,000 instances, d=10, CPU.

The paper reports "<3 s for 500,000 instances on CPU".  This measures the same
configuration on this machine (different CPU) at the paper's t=100 with the
grid-selected m, plus a few reference points.  It is a measurement, not a verdict:
C5 is device-dependent and C6 (GPU) is untestable without a GPU.

Run: python experiments/scalability.py
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead.svead_core import svead_score  # noqa: E402


def run(n=500000, d=10, m_values=(2, 8, 32), t=100, out="results", seed=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    X = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=(n, d))
    res = {"n": int(n), "d": int(d), "generator": "numpy default_rng(0) standard normal",
           "threads": os.environ.get("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "default"), "measurements": []}
    for m in m_values:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        s = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed)
        secs = time.perf_counter() - t0
        res["measurements"].append({
            "m": int(m), "t": int(t), "seconds": secs,
            "seconds_per_1000_instances": secs / n * 1000.0,
            "scores_finite": bool(np.isfinite(s).all()),
            "is_500k_cpu_under_3s": bool(secs < 3.0) if t == 100 else None,
        })
        print("  n=%d d=%d m=%d t=%d -> %.3f s" % (n, d, m, t, secs), flush=True)
    # single-partition reference point (t=1), i.e. the cost of one random Voronoi diagram
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    svead_score(X, m=m_values[0], t=1, seed=seed)
    res["measurements"].append({"m": int(m_values[0]), "t": 1,
                                "seconds": time.perf_counter() - t0,
                                "scores_finite": True, "is_500k_cpu_under_3s": None})
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "scalability.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(res, fh, indent=1)
    return res


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps(run(), indent=1))

per-dataset protocol (m grid {2^1..2^8} capped by n, t=100, 5 repeats, m selected

]

DEFAULT_CAP = 256

def _find(name):
    dirs = []
    env = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if env:
        dirs.append(env)
    dirs.append(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "data"))
    for d in dirs:
        p = os.path.join(d, name)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            return p
    return None


def run(t=100, repeats=5, out="results", time_budget=420.0):
    seeds = SEEDS[:repeats]
    started = time.perf_counter()
    results, skipped = [], []
    for row_name, fname in CANDIDATES:
        p = _find(fname)
        if p is None:
            skipped.append({"dataset": row_name, "why": "not in data cache (no download attempted)"})
            continue
        if time.perf_counter() - started > time_budget:
            skipped.append({"dataset": row_name, "why": "subset time budget exhausted"})
            continue

        n = X.shape[0]
        cap = min(DEFAULT_CAP, int(M_CAP.get(row_name, DEFAULT_CAP)), n)
        m_grid = [m for m in (2 ** i for i in range(1, 9)) if m <= cap]
        per_m = []
        for m in m_grid:

                rocs.append(roc_auc(s, y))
                prs.append(auc_pr_ap(s, y))
            per_m.append({"m": m, "auc_roc": summarize(rocs), "auc_pr_ap": summarize(prs)})
        best_roc = max(per_m, key=lambda r: r["auc_roc"]["mean"])
        best_pr = max(per_m, key=lambda r: r["auc_pr_ap"]["mean"])
        rec = {
            "dataset": row_name, "cache_file": p, "n": int(n), "d": int(X.shape[1]),
            "n_anomalies": int(y.sum()), "anomaly_rate": float(y.mean()),
            "m_grid": m_grid, "t": t, "repeats": repeats,
            "per_m": per_m,
            "selected_m_by_auc_roc": best_roc["m"],
            "auc_roc": best_roc["auc_roc"],
            "auc_pr_at_roc_selected_m": [r for r in per_m if r["m"] == best_roc["m"]][0]["auc_pr_ap"],
            "selected_m_by_auc_pr": best_pr["m"],
            "auc_pr": best_pr["auc_pr_ap"],
        }
        results.append(rec)
        print("  %-16s n=%5d d=%4d m*=%3d AUC-ROC %.4f AUC-PR %.4f"
              % (row_name, n, X.shape[1], best_roc["m"], best_roc["auc_roc"]["mean"],
                 rec["auc_pr_at_roc_selected_m"]["mean"]), flush=True)

    payload = {
        "scope": "spot check on cached ADBench artifacts; NOT the 45-dataset average",
        "config": {"t": t, "m_grid_rule": "{2^1..2^8} capped by n and by the cost guard",
                   "m_cap": dict(M_CAP, default=DEFAULT_CAP), "repeats": repeats},
        "datasets": results,
        "skipped": skipped,
        "n_datasets_run": len(results),
        "subset_mean_auc_roc": (float(np.mean([r["auc_roc"]["mean"] for r in results]))
                                if results else None),
        "subset_mean_auc_pr": (float(np.mean([r["auc_pr_at_roc_selected_m"]["mean"]
                                              for r in results])) if results else None),
        "wall_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started,
    }
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "subset_datasets.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(payload, fh, indent=1)
    return payload


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps(run(), indent=1))
